title: optimize: reduce CPU-side bottlenecks in request path (serialization, thread pools, pinning, KV cache)
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Reduced CPU-side request latency by ~28% and increased small-prompt throughput by ~18% via request-path optimizations: zero-copy serialization, per-core executors with CPU pinning, sharded KV cache, and continuous-batcher improvements. Rollout: canary -> 100% with feature flag; monitor cpu_request_p99, batch_wait_ms, kv_lock_contention.
body:
Context and motivation: Production flamegraphs for the serving runtime showed that a significant fraction of request-side latency was spent on CPU-side bookkeeping: request serialization, global thread-pool contention, and KV cache locking. These bottlenecks are especially visible for short prompts and high-QPS workloads where GPU time per request is small and CPU overhead dominates. This PR aims to reduce CPU-side overhead by optimizing serialization paths, reducing synchronization points in scheduling and KV cache access, and pinning executor threads to cores to improve cache locality.

Summary of changes: implemented zero-copy request header serialization for the hot request path (no intermediate JSON/protobuf stringify for common fields); introduced a per-core executor (worker-local thread pools) with optional CPU affinity pinning and a lightweight work-stealing fallback; replaced the single global KV cache mutex with a sharded cache and fast-path read path using atomics + a thin read-lock for writes; improved the continuous-batcher: pre-allocates batch slots, avoids dynamic allocations on the hot path, and uses a single-writer ring-buffer to enqueue requests to the batcher. Added feature flags (runtime.cpu_request_optimizations) to gate aggressive changes and a soft-fallback to previous behavior.

Benchmarks and results: microbench on c5.12xlarge-like instance simulating small prompts (avg tokens 8): baseline median CPU-side request time 1.8ms, p99 6.2ms. After changes: median 1.3ms (-28%), p99 4.5ms (-27%). End-to-end small-prompt throughput (concurrent clients 500): +18% QPS before hitting GPU saturation. KV lock contention measured with perf_events dropped from ~42% of CPU time to ~8% on the write-heavy synthetic workload. Continuous batcher preallocation reduced allocation-related syscalls by ~95% on the hot path.

Design notes and tradeoffs: per-core executors improve L1/L2 cache locality at the cost of potentially higher core utilization. We keep a work-stealing fallback to avoid starvation. CPU affinity is configurable and disabled by default on containerized environments; the rollout uses a conservative default (enabled on dedicated instances only). Sharded KV cache introduces more shards by default (num_shards = max(16, num_cores/2)) with heuristics to target even distribution; this increases memory slightly but reduces lock contention dramatically. Zero-copy serialization is limited to the small-header common path; large/complex request metadata still follow existing robust path to preserve compatibility.

Testing and validation: unit tests added for sharded KV behavior and continuous batcher correctness; integration tests exercise end-to-end request flow with and without optimizations; perf harness added to redwood/benchmarks/cpu_request_path to reproduce reported numbers. Canary rollout plan described in docs/ops/rollouts.md.

Migration and rollback: changes are behind runtime.cpu_request_optimizations feature flag. To rollback, flip feature flag off; the code provides a compatibility shim to route ongoing in-flight batches back to the global path. Detailed rollback steps are in docs/ops/rollouts.md.

Notes for reviewers: please check the scheduler correctness in scheduler.rs (work-stealing edge cases) and validate the CPU affinity wrapper on macOS/Linux. I included flamegraphs and perf outputs in the benchmark folder for inspection.

review_comments: Diego Rojas: Nice work — design looks solid. A few questions: 1) how do you pick shard count? 2) please add a guard for non-containerized vs containerized to avoid pinning inside k8s unless explicitly enabled.
Asha Patel: answered — shard count is max(16, num_cores/2) with override via config; CPU pinning is disabled by default in containerized environments and we detect cgroups and disable pinning there.
Maya Thompson: CI showed a flaky integration test on first run; please add a retry in the test harness and ensure the batcher shutdown is deterministic.
Asha Patel: fixed — added deterministic shutdown ordering and test retry logic; reran integration tests locally and in CI.
Jun Park: can we add a quick doc note on observability metrics to watch during canary?
Asha Patel: added docs/ops/rollouts.md section with metrics (cpu_request_p99, batch_wait_ms, kv_lock_contention, thread_steal_count) and recommended thresholds.
Maya Thompson: Approve after the added tests and docs.
